project.name: M2.11 rehearsal - Beyond the Horizon
project.brief: Sample target website, not Studio chrome or a real commissioned exhibition. Create an online exhibition companion contrasting observed space photography with imagined space travel. Visitors should browse two entries, read their credits and context, and distinguish a documentary photograph from speculative illustration.
project.audience: Curious non-experts viewing on a phone or desktop; no design or astronomy vocabulary required.
project.purpose: Let each artwork feel distinctive while keeping the catalogue and entry reading experience coherent.
project.constraints: Real source content: Earthrise, Bill Anders/NASA, 24 December 1968; The Grand Tour, Invisible Creature, NASA/JPL-Caltech Visions of the Future. Two routes: catalogue and entry detail. Credits adjacent to each image; readable mobile captions; no copy embedded in images; preserve source image proportions. All references are inspiration only. No assets, direction, fonts or motion are approved. No fabricated exhibition opening date or ticket availability. Rehearsal choices do not establish a permanent user taste profile.

annotations.body: Agent observation: the small Earth, large surrounding dark field, and lunar horizon create a strong contrast in scale. This is one interpretation, not the user's stated preference.
annotations.translation: Give a complete artwork visual priority, with captions outside the image.
annotations.limitations: Image region is an approximate normalized selection on the inspected rendition. No user confirmation or motion observation.

annotations.body:
AGENT PROPOSAL A - QUIET EXHIBITION

Borrow: Earthrise's scale contrast and breathing room. Let one complete artwork lead each entry, with readable captions and a short story. Catalogue uses varied image proportions rather than repeated hero banners.

Leave behind: copying the photograph's black field into every page or treating every work as a space backdrop.

Tradeoff: gives art and reading room, but feels less immediately graphic than B. Keep one strong display title if useful; do not shrink navigation or captions to get that effect.

Status: proposal only. No user choice recorded.
Question: should the catalogue feel primarily contemplative or energetic?
annotations.limitations: Awaiting actual human correction; neither proposal is selected or approved.

decision.rationale: Proposed translation only; compare with the user before deciding.

annotations.body: Agent observation: the poster layers coloured circular forms with horizontal paths; a large title anchors the lower part of the complete image. The selected region shows the layered illustration, not a motion sequence. This is an interpretation, not the user's stated preference.
annotations.borrowedQuality: Layered graphic rhythm and strong title hierarchy
annotations.translation: Use graphic chapter markers and an expressive catalogue title while keeping entry reading calm.
annotations.limitations: Image region is an approximate normalized selection on the inspected rendition. No user confirmation or motion observation.

annotations.body:
AGENT PROPOSAL B - GRAPHIC CATALOGUE

Borrow: Grand Tour's layered shapes, strong title and repeated directional rhythm. Translate this into chapter markers and a distinctive catalogue header; keep credits and entry reading calm.

Leave behind: tracing the poster layout, forcing its full palette into controls, or moving every horizontal line. Static artwork does not establish a motion recipe.

Tradeoff: more recognisable graphic identity, but dense overlays could compete with the artwork or wrap poorly on phones.

Early critique: a generic dark space hero plus glowing gradient cards would flatten both sources into a familiar template. Compare source-specific scale or graphic rhythm instead. Dark backgrounds remain an option if chosen for a reason.

Status: proposal only. No user choice recorded.
